description.narrative:
The HSJF is a mechanism for Development Partners (DPs) to channel resources outside government treasury with oversight of an independent fund manager (the Fiduciary and Procurement Oversight Agent-FPOA), for pre-agreed government priorities. The mechanism is being implemented in Malawi, Africa.
The modality was conceived to combine the merits of sector budget support while providing additional safeguards against fiduciary risk. The main objective of the HSJF is to contribute to the financing of the Malawi Health Sector Strategic Plan for it to achieve its Goal of moving towards UHC by improving the health status, financial risk protection and client satisfaction for all Malawians. Currently, the strategic plan in operation is the HSSP III (2023-2030).
Outcomes: The HSSP III aims to improve health outcomes through the provision of a basic health package (BHP) and health systems strengthening for efficient delivery of the BHP. The HSSP III has a well-defined Health Benefits Package (HBP), previously referred to as Essential Health Package (EHP), to maximize population health within limited available resources. To be more focused, more of RNE’s support will go towards SRHR, Service Level Agreements (SLAs), Direct Facility Financing (DFF) and program Management and support. Most women and adolescent girls face challenges in accessing SRHR services owing to long distances to health facilities. The agreement enables the Ministry of Health to provide SRHR outreach services in hard to rich areas thereby reducing this access barrier to SRHR services among women and adolescent girls. The SLAs provide opportunity for women to access subsidized ante-natal, labour and post-natal services. Subsidized medical services are also provided to new borns and children under the age of 12 years.
